幹線Route Spines

Nine spines. Each is an order of cities, and every decision belongs to a city or to the leg between two cities: which cities and which way round, one city's own extra night, the ryokan and stop towns that sit on a leg, and how the trip ends. Click an option and the map and list change. Nights start at each place's usual count; nudge them with the steppers. Travel times are the kit's researched legs, rounded to five minutes.

Key CITYRYOKANSTOPENDthe kinds of decision — each sits under the city or the leg it belongs to ·blue rail = city · vermilion rail = ryokan · legs read 2h45 train, dashed = flight

Where the decisions live

Which citiesThe major cities and their order. Kyoto, Osaka, or Kyoto and Osaka; start in Tokyo or fly straight into the region; which way round.
A city's own nightOne extra night that belongs to a city and is a yes or a no: Nikkō out and back from Tokyo, Nara after Kyoto, Miyajima off Hiroshima, Kirishima above Kagoshima, Amakusa past Kumamoto.
What sits on a legEach leg between two cities carries its own ryokan and stop towns, each a yes or a no — so a ryokan before a city and one after it are two answers, not one either/or. The specific ryokan is chosen later, so towns only an expert would separate are one option here.
How the trip endsFly home from the last city, end on a ryokan night, or go back through Tokyo for a Haneda ticket.

What is deliberately not a spine

  • Without Tokyo is a choice on spines 5 to 9, not a separate idea: fly straight into the region on a second visit.
  • Nikkō is a ryokan option on 1, 3 and 4: an out-and-back from Tokyo before the trip heads on.
  • Hakone, the Fuji lakes and Izu are one option, "near Mount Fuji": the ryokan decides the town. Same for the Kaga towns, the snow-country valleys, and Amagase or Kurokawa before Yufuin.
  • Okinawa and Shikoku have cards but no routes.
